title: Can I Run DeepSeek-R1 32B on M4 Pro 48GB? VRAM & Speed Calculator

verdict_summary: Apple M4 Pro with 48GB unified memory smoothly runs DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-32B up to Q6_K at 8K context, delivering ~9.7 tok/s at Q4_K_M and scaling cleanly all the way to 64K context.

context_analysis.bottleneck_summary: Unlike 24 GB discrete GPUs, the 48 GB M4 Pro (37.4 GB macOS Metal wired budget by default) has plenty of headroom at Q4_K_M: 19.88 GB weights plus 0.99 GB runtime buffer leave 16.53 GB for KV cache—enough for a full 64K FP16 context (16.00 GB KV) without overflowing. The real limiter is the 273 GB/s unified memory bandwidth, capping speed around ~9.7 tok/s at Q4_K_M.
key_points: DeepSeek-R1 32B Q4_K_M reaches 64K context (16.00 GB FP16 KV cache) at 36.87 GB total, inside the 37.4 GB wired ceiling.
Q6_K (27.06 GB weights, 30.05 GB total at 8K) runs smoothly at ~7.3 tok/s with room up to 32K context using Q8_0 KV.
Q8_0 (34.85 GB weights, 37.84 GB total at 8K) slightly exceeds the default 37.4 GB wired limit, risking swap pressure (~3.2 tok/s).
Prompt prefill on 32K+ codebases takes longer than NVIDIA Tensor Cores, though Metal Flash Attention helps.
optimization_tips: Choose Q6_K for coding/math fidelity (~7.3 tok/s) or Q4_K_M for ~9.7 tok/s reading speed and 64K context.
Enable OLLAMA_FLASH_ATTENTION=1 and OLLAMA_KV_CACHE_TYPE=q8_0 to halve the 1.00 GB per 4K KV growth.
Raise sysctl iogpu.wired_limit_mb=40960 only when experimenting with Q8_0 at 8K–16K context.

faq.question: How fast does DeepSeek-R1 32B run on a MacBook Pro M4 Pro 48GB?
faq.answer: At Q4_K_M with 8K context, expect roughly 9.7 tokens/sec driven by the M4 Pro's 273 GB/s LPDDR5X memory bandwidth—comfortable reading speed even during long reasoning chains.

faq.question: Should I run Q4_K_M, Q6_K, or Q8_0 on M4 Pro 48GB?
faq.answer: Pick Q4_K_M when speed and 32K–64K context matter most (~9.7 tok/s), or Q6_K (~7.3 tok/s) for higher precision at 8K–16K. Avoid Q8_0 unless you raise macOS's default wired GPU limit.

faq.question: Can M4 Pro 48GB handle 64K context on DeepSeek-R1 32B?
faq.answer: Yes. At Q4_K_M, a full 64K FP16 KV cache adds 16.00 GB for a 36.87 GB total footprint, fitting just under macOS's default 37.4 GB wired GPU ceiling.

faq.question: Why does macOS reserve ~10.6 GB out of 48 GB unified memory?
faq.answer: By default macOS caps GPU wired allocations around 75–78% of system RAM so macOS windowing, IDEs, and background apps do not starve or trigger kernel panics.

Max Smooth context with default FP16 KV cache is 8,192 tokens; 12K+ spills layers onto system RAM over PCIe.
Enabling --cache-type-k q8_0 --cache-type-v q8_0 cuts KV cache VRAM in half (~0.50 GB per 4K), stretching Q4_K_M cleanly to 16K–24K.
DeepSeek-R1 emits verbose <think> chains before answering, so monitor context length on multi-file prompts.
optimization_tips: Pass -fa on --cache-type-k q8_0 --cache-type-v q8_0 in llama.cpp to unlock 16K+ context inside 24 GB VRAM.
Close browser hardware acceleration or desktop GPU monitors if free VRAM dips below 23.0 GB on Windows/Linux.
Stick to Q4_K_M; Q5_K_M (23.37 GB weights alone) overflows 24 GB immediately and drops speed below 6 tok/s.

faq.question: Can an RTX 4090 24GB run DeepSeek-R1 32B without spilling to system RAM?
faq.answer: Yes, in Q4_K_M quantization (19.88 GB weights). At 8K context with FP16 KV cache, total VRAM usage is 22.88 GB out of 23.5 GB usable GDDR6X, keeping all 64 transformer layers on GPU at ~37.6 tok/s.

faq.question: What happens if I try Q5_K_M or Q6_K of DeepSeek-R1 32B on the RTX 4090?
faq.answer: Q5_K_M weights alone require 23.37 GB (26.36 GB total at 8K), forcing ~10 layers onto system RAM over PCIe and cutting throughput down to ~5–6 tok/s.

faq.question: How can I reach 16K+ context on RTX 4090 for long DeepSeek-R1 thinking blocks?
faq.answer: Set OLLAMA_FLASH_ATTENTION=1 and OLLAMA_KV_CACHE_TYPE=q8_0 (or -fa on --cache-type-k q8_0 --cache-type-v q8_0 in llama.cpp). Cutting KV memory in half keeps 16K context inside 23.5 GB.

faq.question: Is RTX 4090 faster than an Apple M4 Pro 48GB for DeepSeek-R1 32B?
faq.answer: Yes for decode speed: the RTX 4090's 1,008 GB/s GDDR6X bus achieves ~37.6 tok/s in Q4_K_M, nearly 4x faster than M4 Pro (273 GB/s, ~9.7 tok/s), though M4 Pro can hold 64K context smoothly.

With 15.5 GB usable VRAM and 2.99 GB consumed by 8K KV cache + CUDA runtime buffers, only 12.51 GB remains for weights (~40 of 64 layers). The remaining 24 layers execute on CPU and system DDR4/DDR5 RAM, turning the ~35 GB/s host memory bus into the dominant bottleneck.
key_points: Each 4K of FP16 context consumes 1.00 GB of precious VRAM, directly evicting ~3.2 GPU layers.
Every layer offloaded to system RAM incurs ~8x lower bandwidth (35 GB/s CPU vs 288 GB/s GDDR6).
Q6_K (30.05 GB) drops GPU residency below 50% (~2.1 tok/s), while Q8_0 hits practical OOM.
Make sure your desktop PC has at least 32 GB of dual-channel DDR4/DDR5 RAM before attempting Partial Offload.
optimization_tips: Cap context at 4K–8K and enable Q8_0 KV cache (`--cache-type-k q8_0 --cache-type-v q8_0`) so 43+ layers stay on GPU.
Pin `-ngl 40` explicitly in llama.cpp and pass `-t <physical_cores>` (not hyperthreads) for optimal CPU layer speed.
For interactive IDE coding on RTX 4060 Ti 16GB, Qwen2.5-Coder-14B (Q6_K or Q5_K_M) fits 100% in VRAM at 15–20 tok/s.

faq.question: Can an RTX 4060 Ti 16GB run Qwen2.5-Coder-32B at all?
faq.answer: Yes, via Partial Offload in Q4_K_M (~40/64 layers on GPU and ~24 layers in system RAM). Expect ~3.7 tok/s at 8K context if your host PC has at least 32 GB of dual-channel RAM.

faq.question: Why is Qwen2.5-Coder-32B slow on the RTX 4060 Ti 16GB?
faq.answer: Because ~7.37 GB of weights must be streamed from system RAM across the CPU memory controller (~35 GB/s) on every single generated token, overshadowing the 288 GB/s GPU memory.

faq.question: How many GPU layers (-ngl) should I set for Qwen2.5-Coder-32B on 16GB VRAM?
faq.answer: Start with -ngl 40 at 8K context (or -ngl 43 at 4K context with Q8_0 KV cache). If CUDA reports an out-of-memory allocation error, step -ngl down by 2 layers until stable.

faq.question: Is Qwen2.5-Coder-14B better than 32B on an RTX 4060 Ti 16GB?
faq.answer: For daily interactive coding, yes: Qwen2.5-Coder-14B Q6_K fits completely in 16 GB VRAM with zero CPU offload, generating tokens 4x faster while supporting 16K–32K context.

title: Can I Run Llama-3.3 70B on RTX 3060 12GB? VRAM & Speed Calculator

context_analysis.bottleneck_summary: Llama-3.3-70B packs 70.6B parameters across 80 layers, totaling 42.80 GB in Q4_K_M weights alone. Adding 8K FP16 KV cache (2.50 GB) and runtime overhead (1.56 GB) pushes the total to 46.86 GB. Subtracting KV cache and runtime buffers leaves just 7.44 GB on an RTX 3060 12GB—barely enough for 13 of 80 layers (17.4%), forcing over 35 GB of weights onto slow host RAM.
key_points: Over 35.3 GB of weights must reside in system RAM (requiring 64 GB host RAM to avoid OS disk swap).
CPU-bound execution on 67 offloaded layers drops generation below ~1.5 tok/s even on fast DDR5 systems.
Each 4K of FP16 context consumes 1.25 GB of VRAM, quickly eating the RTX 3060's remaining capacity.
Even extreme 2-bit quants (IQ2_XXS, ~20 GB) still exceed 12 GB VRAM by a wide margin.
optimization_tips: Switch to Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct (Q8_0) or DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-14B (Q4_K_M), which fit inside 12 GB VRAM.
If you must test 70B locally with an RTX 3060, ensure 64 GB system RAM and try IQ2_XS with -ngl 22 for batch runs.
For smooth 70B inference, step up to dual RTX 3090 (48 GB total VRAM) or an Apple Mac Studio with 64 GB+ RAM.

faq.question: Can an RTX 3060 12GB run Llama-3.3-70B?
faq.answer: Practically no (OOM for GPU residency). Q4_K_M requires 46.86 GB at 8K context, so only ~17.4% (13/80 layers) fits on the RTX 3060, forcing almost all inference onto your CPU and system RAM.

faq.question: How much system RAM would I need to CPU-offload Llama-3.3-70B alongside an RTX 3060?
faq.answer: You need at least 64 GB of dual-channel DDR4/DDR5 system RAM just to hold the remaining 35+ GB of weights plus OS overhead without crashing or thrashing an NVMe pagefile.

faq.question: What is the largest Llama or Qwen model that runs smoothly on an RTX 3060 12GB?
faq.answer: 14B-class models (like DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-14B or Qwen2.5-Coder-14B) at Q4_K_M (~10.7 GB total at 4K–8K context) fit 100% in 12 GB VRAM and run smoothly around 23–26 tok/s.

faq.question: What hardware is needed to run Llama-3.3-70B smoothly at 8K+ context?
faq.answer: You need over 47 GB of usable GPU/unified memory—for example an Apple M1/M2/M3/M4 Max 64GB, or dual 24 GB NVIDIA GPUs (2x RTX 3090 or 2x RTX 4090).
